title: A slow reader puts old data back in the cache, and how a lease stops it
captions: Reader A asks the cache for key k and misses. The cache gives A a lease: a token that A must show when it puts a value back.
A reads the database and gets v1. Then A is slow for a moment, for example because of a long pause or a slow network.
Writer B updates the database to v2 and deletes k from the cache. The delete also cancels A's lease, L1.
A finally sends set k = v1. Without leases the cache accepts it. Now the cache holds old data. It stays until the TTL ends or the next write deletes it.
With leases, the cache checks L1, sees it was cancelled, and rejects the set. The next reader misses and loads v2.
